Consider the circle of radius $10$ centered at the origin, as shown above. Construct a set of parametric equations, defined for $\theta \in [0,2\pi ),$ that traverse the circle once in the counterclockwise direction starting at the point $A(10,0).$

$x=$
{{field-1}}$,\,y=$
{{field-2}}$,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi )$
worked_solution:
The parametric equations of a circle of radius $r$ centered at the origin are

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

Under this parametrization, the circle is traversed once in the counterclockwise direction, starting from $(r,0).$

In our case, the radius is $r=10.$ Substituting $r=10$ gives

$$
x=10\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=10\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$
